EXPERIENCE (PRD): I have had issues with my platelets being low for about 4 years.  There was a mass in my spleen but the oncologist said almost no one gets cancer in their spleen. So, hematologist monitored it and since the mass did not change and blood work did not get worse, he said to return if platelets got down to 60,000.  I became anemic last September and platelets were 90,000. So when we did repeat bloodwork in February platelets were down to 78,000 so we decided to return to hematologist/now oncologist and he did a PET scan and bone marrow biopsy which showed little concern because the highest metabolic number was a 7. Doctor decided to refer to surgeon in May. Surgeon said we don't leave spleens in you when they have a hard mass, so scheduled surgery for August 7, 2019.  When spleen was removed Wichita hospital pathologists believed it was just a hemangioma, but sent samples to Mayo clinic where it was diagnosed an angiosarcoma with metastasizing lesions to the edge of my liver.  I was referred to Mayo and am now waiting for an appointment to be scheduled.  The lesions on my liver are numerous but are only evident on the edge of my liver. PET scan in may only showed a small area on the top of my spleen that had a metabolic growth number of 6 & 7.  It did show also a #6 on my neck which they believed could be arthritis.  I have had pain in my neck and in my lower back for years so we are hoping it is arthritis.  Oncologist believes that my particular angiosarcoma has grown slower than most and that removing the spleen removed 95% of the active tumor at least. The liver lesions were noted on the pathology report to be similar in structure to the spleen tissue so then they noted it was considered metastasizing lesions.
